newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite activist.
newsitem.headline: Gunmen kill Pakistani Shi'ite activist.

text.p: Masked gunmen killed a Pakistani Shi'ite Moslem activist on Tuesday in the central province of Punjab in an apparent sectarian attack, police said.

They said the gunmen shot Tabassum Raza, a doctor, with automatic weapons in the evening while he was treating patients at his clinic at Lodhran town, some 75 km (45 miles) north of the main southern Punjab city of Multan, and then escaped.
Raza, the district financial secretary of the Shi'ite Tehrik-i-Jafaria party, died later in hospital.
Nobody claimed responsibility for the killing, the latest in a series attacks that rival militants from the majority Sunni Moslems and the minority Shi'ites blamed on each other.
A long-running feud between the militant Sunni and Shi'ite groups cost more than 170 lives in Pakistan last year.

Sunni-Shi'ite disputes over Islamic beliefs have often spilled into violence in Pakistan. Sunnis dominate Pakistan's population of more than 130 million, while Shi'ites are about 15 percent but are the majority in neighbouring Iran.
